title: 164 years, 31 moments
lede: From a Baltimore toy shop to a storefront on Amazon. Filter by thread.

events.title: Founded in Baltimore
events.text: Frederick August Otto Schwarz opens a toy shop six years after arriving from Westphalia.

events.title: Moves to New York
events.text: The Schwarz Toy Bazaar opens on Broadway.

events.title: 745 Fifth Avenue
events.text: After several moves the store settles on Fifth Avenue.

events.title: The family sells
events.text: The Schwarz family sells the firm to Parents’ Magazine.

events.title: W.R. Grace
events.text: Parents’ sells the company to W.R. Grace & Co.

events.title: Franz Carl Weber
events.text: The Zurich toy retailer buys the company.

events.title: Christiana, then Harris and Morse
events.text: Christiana Companies pays $10.5M. Months later its president, Peter L. Harris, and Peter C. Morse buy the company.

events.title: 767 Fifth Avenue opens
events.text: The flagship moves across the street into 40,000 square feet at the foot of the General Motors Building.

events.title: “Big”
events.text: The film shows the store’s floor piano. Requests for the $15,000 instrument follow.

events.title: Sold to KBB
events.text: The Dutch retailer Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer pays an estimated $40M.

events.title: 39 locations
events.text: Large stores are readied for Orlando and Las Vegas, and the Manhattan store prepares to grow to 60,000 square feet.

events.title: Vendex takes over KBB
events.text: Vendex International becomes the owner.

events.title: Right Start agrees to buy
events.text: The Right Start announces a deal for the flagship, 22 other stores, the catalog and the website. The trade press values it at $55M.

events.title: The deal closes
events.text: The buyer pays with $15.95M of notes and $20.0M of preferred stock.

events.title: Renamed FAO Inc.
events.text: The Right Start takes the name of its acquisition. It runs 23 FAO Schwarz, 64 Right Start and 169 Zany Brainy stores.

events.title: Suppliers stop shipping
events.text: Several major suppliers have stopped shipping. FAO Inc. says it will close 55 Zany Brainy stores.

events.title: First Chapter 11
events.text: FAO Inc. and its main subsidiaries file in Delaware, listing $257.4M of assets and $238.4M of debts.

events.title: Out of bankruptcy
events.text: The plan takes effect after 111 store closings, with $30.0M of new preferred stock and a $77.0M credit facility.

events.title: “Not experiencing a cash crunch”
events.text: FAO Inc. denies a New York Post report about its cash position.

events.title: Notice of default
events.text: The company says holiday sales are “significantly below expectations.” Its lenders deliver a notice of default the same afternoon.

events.title: Second Chapter 11
events.text: FAO Inc. files again, to sell FAO Schwarz and The Right Start and liquidate Zany Brainy. Its shares are delisted.

events.title: Sale approved
events.text: The court approves the sale of the brand and the New York and Las Vegas stores to a D. E. Shaw affiliate for $40.5M in cash.

events.title: Las Vegas reopens
events.text: The Forum Shops store reopens after remodeling. New York is scheduled to follow on Thanksgiving Day.

events.title: The old parent deregisters
events.text: Children’s Books & Toys, Inc., as FAO Inc. was renamed, files to end its SEC registration.

events.title: Toys “R” Us buys it
events.text: The parent of Toys “R” Us acquires the business for an undisclosed price.

events.title: Closing announced
events.text: Toys “R” Us says the Fifth Avenue store will close, citing rising costs.

events.title: The flagship closes
events.text: The last FAO Schwarz store shuts. The brand continues online and on toys in Toys “R” Us stores.

events.title: Sold to ThreeSixty Group
events.text: Terms are not disclosed. Toys “R” Us books a $45M gain.

events.title: 30 Rockefeller Plaza
events.text: A new 20,000 square foot flagship opens.

events.title: A shop inside Nordstrom
events.text: FAO Schwarz opens in Nordstrom’s Manhattan flagship on West 57th Street.

events.title: Amazon storefront
events.text: The company says it has stores in New York, Paris, Milan and Beijing.
